sources.citation: Karim, Shuan Osman & Saloumeh Gholami (eds.). 2024. Gorani in its Historical and Linguistic Context. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton (CC BY-NC-ND). DOI 10.1515/9783111168852.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: downloaded (Internet Archive copy of the OAPEN PDF, 293 pp., text layer). Bajalani appears 19 times: classification (ch.1: 'Little evidence suggests that Shabaki and Bajalani are linguistically distinct entities. According to MacKenzie (1956), the distinction is between Shabaki, the language and Bajalani, the tribe'), ethnonyms (Mačo), plural -gel, enumerative -a. Stress is discussed only for Hawrami/Bzɫāna/Gawraju gender-marking vowels; nothing on Bajalani stress.

sources.citation: MacKenzie, D. N. 2002. GURĀNI. Encyclopaedia Iranica XI/4: 401-403. https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/gurani/
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Read in full (the Internet Archive 2026-08-15; live site could not be reached by automated download). General Gurāni sketch; the only stress remark is that most dialects 'share with the neighboring Kurdish two stressed determinative suffixes, masc. -ak'a, fem. Hawr. -ak'ē, Kand. -ak'ī, and in combination with a demonstrative adjective -'a'; Bajalani pronouns are given with stress marks (Bāj. am'in, at'ū, ēm'a, ēšm'a, ēš'ān) but no rule of word-stress placement is stated.

sources.citation: Leezenberg, Michiel. 1993. Gorani influence on Central Kurdish: substratum or prestige borrowing? ILLC Prepublication X-93-03. Amsterdam: University of Amsterdam.

sources.note: Open PDF (image-only; scanned at 300 dpi.). Sociolinguistic/historical paper; gives a few Bajalani (MacKenzie 1956, Arpachi informant) vs Shabak lexical contrasts and quotes MacKenzie 1956: 419-420 ('All Shabaks.. called themselves Bajlan or Bējwan'). Nothing on stress.
